plan: [ This mechanism is equivalent to a second-price auction: highest sealed bid wins and pays the second-highest bid. With independent private values and no future linkage, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Bidding above risks negative payoff if you win and pay more than value; bidding below risks losing when winning would be profitable. Therefore, to maximize expected profit this round (and in the long run in similar rounds), bid exactly your value: 23. ]

[ This is strategically equivalent to a sealed-bid second-price auction because the winner pays the second-highest sealed bid. With independent private values, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy: overbidding risks paying more than your value; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. There is no prior history to exploit and only one round, so maximize expected profit by setting the exit price equal to my value. My value is 18, so I bid 18. ]

[ This is strategically equivalent to a second‑price (Vickrey) auction where the winner pays the second-highest sealed bid. The dominant strategy is to bid my true value to maximize expected profit. Underbidding risks losing profitable wins; overbidding risks winning and paying above value if a rival’s bid lies between my value and my inflated bid. With value 25 and no learning across rounds (only 1 round), I bid 25 to ensure I win exactly when price ≤ my value and avoid negative surplus. ]
